AO: Aircraft Operator - The organization or entity responsible for the operation of an aircraft, including airlines, charter operators, and private operators.
APCH: Approach - The phase of flight during which an aircraft descends toward an airport for landing, following a specified approach procedure (instrument or visual).
APN: Apron - A defined area on an airport intended for aircraft parking, loading/unloading, refueling, and maintenance activities.
APR: April - The fourth month of the year, used in date notations within NOTAM and aviation documentation.
APRX: Approximate or Approximately - A term used to indicate that a value, time, or location is not exact but close to the stated figure.
APSG: After Passing - A term used in navigation and ATC clearances to indicate actions to be taken after crossing a specified point or fix.
APU: Auxiliary Power Unit - A self-contained unit on an aircraft that provides electrical power and pneumatic pressure for engine starting and ground operations without running the main engines.
ARC: Area Chart - An aeronautical chart depicting a specific terminal area, showing airspace structure, navigation aids, and arrival/departure procedures.
ARNG: Arrange - A term used in aviation communications to request or confirm the coordination of services, schedules, or operational procedures.
ARQ: Automatic Error Correction - A data transmission mode that automatically detects and corrects errors in received messages, used in aeronautical telecommunications.
AS: Altostratus - A mid-level cloud type forming a gray or blue-gray sheet that often covers the entire sky, sometimes producing light precipitation.
ASAP: As Soon As Possible - An abbreviation used in aviation communications to indicate urgency in completing a requested action without specifying an exact deadline.
ASC: Ascend To or Ascending To - An instruction or description indicating that an aircraft is climbing to a specified altitude or flight level.
ASE: Altimetry System Error - The difference between the altitude indicated by an aircraft's altimeter system and the true altitude, caused by instrument or pressure setting errors.
ASPH: Asphalt - A pavement material used for runway, taxiway, and apron surfaces, commonly found at many aerodromes worldwide.
ATA: Actual Time of Arrival - The precise time at which an aircraft arrives at a specified point, such as a waypoint or the landing runway threshold.
ATD: Actual Time of Departure - The precise time at which an aircraft departs from a specified point, such as the gate or takeoff point.
ATFM: Air Traffic Flow Management - A service designed to balance air traffic demand with available airspace and airport capacity to ensure safe and efficient traffic flow.
ATM: Air Traffic Management - The dynamic, integrated management of air traffic and airspace, including air traffic services, airspace management, and traffic flow management.
ATN: Aeronautical Telecommunication Network - A global digital data network designed to support air-ground and ground-ground communications for air traffic management and airline operations.
ATTN: Attention - A term used in aviation communications to draw focus to important information or to request careful consideration of a message.
ATZ: Aerodrome Traffic Zone - A designated airspace around an aerodrome where special rules apply to protect aircraft operating in the vicinity.
AUG: August - The eighth month of the year, used in date notations within NOTAM and aviation documentation.
AUTH: Authorized or Authorization - The granting of permission for a specific action, operation, or access in aviation operations.
AUTO: Automatic - A descriptor indicating that a system or process operates without human intervention, such as automatic weather observation systems.
AUW: All Up Weight - The total weight of an aircraft including the aircraft itself, fuel, payload, crew, and passengers at a given time.
AUX: Auxiliary - A secondary or backup system or component that supports the primary system in aircraft operations.
AVBL: Available or Availability - A term indicating that a facility, service, or resource is accessible and ready for use.
AVG: Average - The arithmetic mean of a set of values, used in wind reporting, temperature data, and other aviation statistical information.
AVGAS: Aviation Gasoline - A high-octane fuel used in piston-engine aircraft, distinct from jet fuel (kerosene) used in turbine engines.
AWTA: Advise At What Time Able - A request in aviation communications for a pilot to report the time at which they will be able to comply with an instruction or clearance.
AWY: Airway - A designated corridor of airspace through which aircraft operate, defined by navigation aids and waypoints, typically 10 nautical miles wide.
AZM: Azimuth - The angular measurement of a bearing relative to true north, used in navigation and radar positioning.
BA: Braking Action - A report describing the effectiveness of aircraft braking on a runway surface, reported as good, medium, poor, or nil.
BCFG: Fog Patches - Patches of fog covering only portions of an aerodrome, reducing visibility in localized areas while other areas remain clear.
BCST: Broadcast - The transmission of information or instructions to multiple receivers simultaneously, such as ATIS or VOLMET broadcasts.
BDRY: Boundary - The defined limit of an airspace, control area, or other aviation-related geographical area.
BECMG: Becoming - A term used in weather forecasts (TAF) to indicate an expected change in weather conditions during a specified time period.
BFR: Before - A term used in aviation communications to indicate a time or event preceding a specified reference point or action.
BKN: Broken - A cloud coverage descriptor indicating that 5/8 to 7/8 of the sky is covered by clouds, reported in METAR and aviation weather observations.
BLDG: Building - A structure on or near an aerodrome that may be referenced as a visual landmark or obstacle in aeronautical charts.
BLO: Below Clouds - A flight condition or altitude reference indicating that an aircraft is operating beneath the cloud layer.
BLW: Below - A term used to indicate a position or value lower than a specified reference point, such as altitude below minimums.
BOMB: Bombing - Military training activity involving the release of practice or live munitions, typically conducted within designated restricted airspace.
BR: Mist - A weather phenomenon consisting of suspended water droplets or wet haze reducing visibility to between 1,000 and 5,000 meters.
BRG: Bearing - The horizontal direction from one point to another, expressed in degrees relative to true or magnetic north.
BRKG: Braking - The act or quality of decelerating an aircraft on the ground, related to braking action reports and aircraft braking system performance.
BS: Commercial Broadcasting Station - A ground-based radio station used for commercial broadcasting, which may be referenced as a navigation aid or potential source of radio interference.
BTL: Between Layers - A flight condition where an aircraft is operating in the airspace between two distinct cloud layers.
BTN: Between - A term used to define a range or interval between two specified points, times, or values in aviation communications.
